literal_statement:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^d$ be a bounded convex domain and let $\xi_0\in\partial\Omega$. A holomorphic self-map is a holomorphic map $f:\Omega\to\Omega$. The tangent cone of $\overline{\Omega}$ at $\xi_0$ determines the proposed order $m=m(\xi_0)$. **Convex-domain boundary rigidity conjecture.** The number $m=m(\xi_0)$ depends only on the tangent cone of $\overline{\Omega}$ at $\xi_0$, and every holomorphic self-map satisfying

$$
f(z)=z+o\left(\left\|z-\xi_0\right\|^m\right)
$$

must be the identity: $f=\operatorname{id}$. This would extend the paper’s boundary Schwarz lemma for bounded convex domains with $C^2$ boundary to arbitrary bounded convex domains and clarify how the tangent-cone geometry controls the optimal error term; the conjecture is presented without a resolution.
technical_assessment: For every bounded convex domain and boundary point, tangent-cone-dependent finite order must force identity; corner and nonsmooth boundary estimates are essential. No uniform local-to-global rigidity mechanism established.
title: Convex-domain boundary rigidity conjecture

literal_statement:
Let $C_1$ be the hyperelliptic curve

$$
y^2=x^{2g+2}+c,
$$

where $g=2k$ is its genus and $c$ is the constant appearing in the defining equation. Let $\operatorname{ST}^0(C_1)$ denote the identity component of the Sato–Tate group of the Jacobian of $C_1$. **Even-genus Sato–Tate group conjecture.** One has

$$
\operatorname{ST}^0(C_1)=\underbrace{\operatorname{U}(1)_2\times\operatorname{U}(1)_2\times\cdots\times\operatorname{U}(1)_2}_{k\text{ times}}.
$$

The formula is motivated by computations using the paper's algorithm for genera $2$, $4$, $6$, and $8$; its validity for all even genera remains conjectural in the supplied text.
technical_assessment: All even genera require a CM Jacobian decomposition and independence of characters; genera 2,4,6,8 do not control arbitrary composite 2g+2. c and smoothness also require primary definitions.
title: Conjectural Sato–Tate group formula for even-genus trinomial hyperelliptic curves

literal_statement:
Let $A$ be a complementary alphabet of size $m$, and let $R(n,m)$ be the set of positive integers $k$ for which there is a word $P$ of length $2n$ over $A$ having exactly $k$ $P$-valid rooted plane trees. **Black–Drellich–Tymoczko's range conjecture.** For all $m$ and $n$, 

$$
R(n,m)=R(n,1).
$$

Equivalently, the possible numbers of valid plane trees depend only on $n$, not on the alphabet size $m$. The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is resolved, and the introduction explicitly says it is false by giving a counterexample for $n=7$; hence the conjecture is refuted.
technical_assessment: Literal statement itself reports a published n=7 counterexample to all-m,n equality. No new witness credit; actual source proof body not inspected here.
title: Black–Drellich–Tymoczko's range conjecture for valid plane trees

literal_statement:
Let $F_n$ be a free group of finite rank $n\geq 2$. A subgroup $R\leq F_n$ is a **retract** of $F_n$ if there is a homomorphism $r:F_n\to R$ whose restriction to $R$ is the identity. A subgroup $H$ of $F_n$ is **inert** if $\operatorname{rk}(K\cap H)\leq \operatorname{rk}(K)$ for every subgroup $K$ of $F_n$.

**Dicks–Ventura conjecture.** Every retract of $F_n$ is inert.

Turner’s argument shows that this is equivalent to the Dicks–Ventura conjecture asserting inertia of fixed subgroups of arbitrary families of endomorphisms. The conjecture is known for fixed subgroups of families of injective endomorphisms, but remains open for arbitrary endomorphisms.
technical_assessment: Every retract must meet every subgroup with rank at most the latter rank. Stallings calculations for a few retracts cannot establish this double universal assertion; no full-scope mechanism.
title: Dicks–Ventura retract inertia conjecture for free groups

literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a 2-dimensional cluster variety, and let $h:Y\to\Delta$ be a Lefschetz $T^2$-fibration over the unit disk such that $Y$ is diffeomorphic to $X$. For a diffeomorphism $f:X\to Y$, write the induced pullback as $f^*:H^*(Y;\mathbb{Q})\to H^*(X;\mathbb{Q})$.

**P=W conjecture.** For any diffeomorphism $f:X\to Y$, the $P=W$ identity holds under $f^*$.

The conjecture asks whether the perverse filtration associated with the Lefschetz fibration is determined by the underlying smooth manifold of the cluster variety. The preceding theorem establishes the identity for elliptic fibrations in a specified deformation family, while the conjecture asserts it for every Lefschetz $T^2$-fibration satisfying the stated diffeomorphism condition.
technical_assessment: Arbitrary diffeomorphisms and Lefschetz fibrations require filtration invariance beyond the specified elliptic deformation family. No short topological identification supplied.
title: The P=W identity for diffeomorphic cluster varieties and Lefschetz torus fibrations

literal_statement: Let a geodesic net in the Euclidean plane have four unbalanced vertices and some number of balanced vertices. **Four-vertex unboundedness conjecture.** There exist geodesic nets in the Euclidean plane with $4$ unbalanced vertices and an arbitrarily large number of balanced vertices. The assertion may already hold when the unbalanced vertices are the vertices of a square. This would show that no bound exists for the number of balanced vertices in terms of four fixed unbalanced vertices, extending the search beyond the known irreducible example with $16$ balanced vertices.
technical_assessment: Arbitrarily many balanced vertices with four unbalanced vertices requires a scalable irreducible net construction under exact source conventions. Subdividing edges might only exploit excluded degree-two vertices; no such credit.
title: Unbounded balanced vertices for planar geodesic nets with four unbalanced vertices

literal_statement: For a positive integer $d$, let $\operatorname{F}(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ be the free group on $X_1,\ldots,X_d$, and let $w\in\operatorname{F}(X_1,\ldots,X_d)$ be a nontrivial word. For a finite group $G$, write $\lambda(G)$ for its nonsolvable length. We say that $w$ is **nonsolvable-length-bounding** if there is a function $f_w:(0,1]\rightarrow[0,\infty]$ such that, for every $\rho\in(0,1]$ and every finite group $G$, whenever some fiber of the word map $w_G:G^d\rightarrow G$ has proportion at least $\rho$, one has $\lambda(G)\leq f_w(\rho)$. **NLB conjecture.** Every nontrivial word is nonsolvable-length-bounding. This conjecture is due to Michael Larsen and is described as very challenging; even the case $\rho=1$, when $w$ is an identity of $G$, is unknown.
technical_assessment: The displayed f_w is allowed value infinity, making a literal bound vacuous. Intended finite bounds for every word and positive density require primary correction and deep finite-group structure; wording correction earns no credit.
title: The NLB conjecture for nontrivial words

literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta$, and let $\mu(G)$ denote its hat chromatic number. **Maximum-degree conjecture.** Every graph $G$ with maximum degree $\Delta$ satisfies

$$
\mu(G)\leqslant \Delta+1.
$$

This would give a universal upper bound on the hat chromatic number in terms of the maximum degree, but the source supplies no resolution.
technical_assessment: Universal hat-game bound by Delta+1 requires a strategy obstruction for all graphs; LLL constants do not reach the target. Same apparent question as assigned 348454; do not count twice.
title: The maximum-degree bound for the hat chromatic number

literal_statement:
Let $b$\mathbb{T}$ be the tropical semiring, and let $UT_n(b$\mathbb{T})$ denote the semigroup of $n\times n$ upper triangular tropical matrices. A semigroup identity is a formal equality of words that holds under every substitution of matrices.

**Strict identity-variety growth conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$, there is a semigroup identity satisfied by $UT_n(b$\mathbb{T})$ but not by $UT_{n+1}(b$\mathbb{T})$.

The paper proves that no single semigroup identity holds for all finite-dimensional upper triangular tropical matrix semigroups, but the stronger assertion that each successive dimension has strictly fewer identities is left as an expectation.
technical_assessment: An identity absent in some larger dimension does not separate each adjacent n,n+1. Need an explicit dimension-sensitive word family and verified substitution; prior r560 plactic result is not by itself that bridge.
title: Strict identity-variety growth conjecture for upper triangular tropical matrices

literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a dual $k$-cell, and let a **Delone tessellation** of a lattice be its tessellation into Delone cells.

**Strong dimension conjecture.** For every dual $k$-cell $D$ there is a $k$-dimensional lattice $\Lambda$ such that there is a $k$-dimensional cell in the Delone tessellation of $\Lambda$ equivalent to $D$.

This is presented as a stronger version of the dimension conjecture. Both conjectures are stated as open, and a counterexample would immediately give a counterexample to the Voronoi conjecture.
technical_assessment: Every dual k-cell must occur in a k-dimensional lattice Delone tessellation. Small-dimensional Voronoi theorems cannot settle unbounded k; no constructive lattice realization route.
title: Strong dimension conjecture for dual cells

literal_statement:
Let $F_Y$ be a free group on the set $Y$, and let $H\leq K\leq F_Y$ be subgroups. For a basis $X$ of $F_Y$, write $\Gamma_X(H)\to\Gamma_X(K)$ for the morphism between the associated core graphs. An extension $H\leq K$ is **algebraic** if it is not contained in any proper free factor of $K$.

**Miasnikov–Ventura–Weil conjecture.** If the morphism

$$
\Gamma_X(H)\to\Gamma_X(K)
$$

is surjective for every basis $X$ of $F_Y$, then $K$ is an algebraic extension of $H$.

The converse is true, but the conjecture itself is refuted by a counterexample in the free group $F_2$ on two generators.
technical_assessment: Literal text reports a free-rank-two counterexample to surjectivity-for-all-bases implying algebraicity. Reproducing it would be public-result reconstruction; body not audited here.
title: Miasnikov–Ventura–Weil algebraic-extension conjecture for free groups

literal_statement:
Let $F_Y$ be a free group on the set $Y$, with subgroups $H\leq K\leq F_Y$. For every basis $X$ of $F_Y$, consider the associated core-graph morphism $\Gamma_X(H)\to\Gamma_X(K)$. An extension $H\leq K$ is **algebraic** if it is not contained in any proper free factor of $K$.

**Rank-greater-than-two conjecture.** The original Miasnikov–Ventura–Weil conjecture holds for $H\leq K\leq F_Y$ whenever $|Y|>2$.

The assertion excludes the known counterexample in rank two, but the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.
technical_assessment: Extending the rank-two free group by a free factor introduces bases mixing old and new generators; universal core-surjectivity need not survive. No routine rank-lift counterexample asserted.
title: Miasnikov–Ventura–Weil conjecture for free groups of rank greater than two

literal_statement:
For permutations $\alpha$ and $\beta$, let $\alpha\ominus\beta$ denote their skew sum, and let $\operatorname{id}_t$ be the identity permutation of length $t$. Let $\Xi(\tau)$ denote the set of finite groups arising in the paper's powerfully pattern-avoiding construction for the pattern $\tau$.

**Finiteness conjecture for decreasing extensions.** For every positive integer $t$, the set

$$
\Xi(\operatorname{id}_t\ominus 1)
$$

is finite.

The conjecture is trivial for $t=1$ and follows from a theorem in the source for $t=2$; the general case remains open in the paper.
technical_assessment: For every t, finiteness of all groups arising from powerfully avoiding id_t skew 1 needs a uniform group-order restriction. Known t=1,2 are parameter instances; no general mechanism.
title: Finiteness conjecture for indecomposable decreasing extensions

literal_statement:
Let $N$ be a natural number. For $k\geq 1$, define the finite rank and crank moments for vector partitions by

$$
N_{k,N}(n):=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}m^kN_{S_1}(m,n),\qquad M_{k,N}(n):=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}m^kM_{S_2}(m,n),
$$

where $N_{S_1}(m,n)$ and $M_{S_2}(m,n)$ are the corresponding finite rank and crank distributions. **Finite moment inequality conjecture.** For any fixed natural number $N$ and even $k\geq 2$,

$$
M_{k,N}(n)>N_{k,N}(n)\quad\text{for all }n\geq 1.
$$

This is the finite analogue of Garvan's rank–crank moment inequality and extends the immediately known case $k=2$ from the finite Andrews identity. The paper's abstract says that the present work proves this conjecture, so it is recorded as solved.
technical_assessment: Literal text reports this source proves every N, even k>=2,n>=1 inequality. Metadata conflicts with that report; no credit and no independently body-verified solution claim here.
title: Finite rank and crank moment inequality conjecture

literal_statement:
For each positive integer $n$, let $\mathcal{S}_\rho$ denote the graded Frobenius characteristic associated with the hook shape $\rho$, let $e_1^\perp$ be the operator adjoint to multiplication by $e_1$, and let $\operatorname{Id}$ be the identity operator. **Skewing conjecture.** For all $n$, 

$$
(\operatorname{Id}\otimes e_1^\perp)\mathcal{S}_{(n)}=\sum_{a=0}^{n-2}\mathcal{S}_{(a\,|\,n-a-2)},
$$

and

$$
(e_1^\perp\otimes\operatorname{Id})\mathcal{S}_{1^n}=\sum_{a=1}^{n-1}\mathcal{S}_{(a\,|\,n-a-1)}.
$$

These identities are reported as confirmed by computations for $n\leq4$, but no proof or general resolution is supplied.
technical_assessment: Both skewing identities for every n require a module-level decomposition or character identity. n<=4 experiments cannot bridge arbitrary hook modules; n=1 boundary conventions require source checking.
title: Skewing identities for hook-indexed modules

literal_statement: Consider the May–Ravenel spectral sequence used to compute the relevant $\mathrm{tmf}$-resolution input for $Z$. **Torsion conjecture.** The May–Ravenel spectral sequence collapses at $E_1$ with no hidden $v_2$-extensions. This is explicitly introduced as an optimistic assumption for analyzing unbounded $v_2$-torsion; its consequences for the $\mathrm{tmf}$-ASS remain conjectural.
technical_assessment: The relevant Z and spectral sequence are not defined in the record; collapse plus absence of hidden extensions is stronger than a finite-page computation. No certificate endpoint available.
title: The May–Ravenel collapse and torsion conjecture

literal_statement:
Let $G_n$ be a sequence of connected graphs, each with $n$ vertices and $O(n^{\alpha})$ edges, where $\alpha<2$ is fixed. Here $P(G)$ denotes the probability that a uniformly chosen subtree of $G$ is spanning. **Chin et al.'s conjecture.** Then

$$
\lim_{n \to \infty}P(G_n)=0.
$$

This conjecture asserts that subquadratic edge growth forces the spanning-subtree probability to vanish. The paper explicitly states that the conjecture is false: a path with a complete graph of order $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$ attached to each end provides a counterexample.
technical_assessment: Literal record supplies the path-with-clique-ends counterexample mechanism to every subquadratic sequence tending to zero. It is explicitly source-derived, not a new asymptotic construction.
title: Chin et al.'s sparse graph conjecture for spanning-subtree probability

literal_statement: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Polish group. A nonempty subset $C\subseteq\mathbb{G}$ is **anti-GMS** if it is nowhere dense and, for every sequence $\{U_n:n\in\omega\}$ of open neighborhoods of the identity, there is a sequence $\{g_n:n\in\omega\}$ in $\mathbb{G}$ such that, for every $g\in\mathbb{G}$, the set $g\cdot\bigcup_{n\in\omega}g_n\cdot U_n$ is dense in $C$. **Strong conjecture.** Exactly one of the following holds for any Polish group $\mathbb{G}$: either $\mathbb{G}$ is locally compact, or it contains an anti-GMS set. Anti-GMS sets are the paper's tool for disproving the Galvin–Mycielski–Solovay theorem in non-locally compact groups; the dichotomy itself remains open.
technical_assessment: For each non-locally-compact Polish group need a single nowhere-dense C handling every neighborhood sequence and all translates. No uniform selection construction or local compactness obstruction proof here.
title: The strong conjecture on anti-GMS sets in Polish groups

literal_statement: Let $N=pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are the prime factors under consideration, and let $\mathbb{Q}$-$\mathcal{KW}(N)$ denote the rational Korselt witness set associated with $N$. **Oddness conjecture.** For all $N=pq$, $\mathbb{Q}$-$\mathcal{KW}(N)$ is odd. The paper presents this as an unsolved issue arising from the study of rational Korselt sets for products of two primes; no resolution is given in the supplied text.
technical_assessment: Primary v1 Definition1.3 defines KS, while Conjecture4.7 says KW is odd without defining KW. Inspected final example and local Main Theorem proof, not all dependencies. Clarify cardinality/notation and inspect cited Q-Korselt pq successor before any investment.
title: Oddness conjecture for the rational Korselt witness set of pq

literal_statement: Let $G$ be a connected $d4f$-regular graph for an infinite cardinal $d4f$, and call an edge-colouring distinguishing if the only colour-preserving automorphism of $G$ is the identity. **The infinite-cardinal distinguishing-index conjecture.** Then $G$ admits a distinguishing edge-colouring with two colours. The source proves this when $d4f$ is a fixed point of the aleph hierarchy and notes that the corresponding class of cardinals is unbounded; the conjecture asks for the result for every infinite cardinal.
technical_assessment: All infinite cardinals go beyond aleph fixed points; extending a two-color symmetry-breaking recursion requires control at singular cardinals. Garbled d4f notation must be checked; no finite certificate route.
title: The infinite-cardinal distinguishing-index conjecture

literal_statement: Let $C_4$ be the $4$-cycle, and let $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_4)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph containing no copy of $C_4$. A **polarity graph** is the graph associated with a polarity of a finite projective plane. **McCuaig's conjecture.** Every extremal graph $G$ with $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_4)$ edges is a subgraph of some polarity graph.
technical_assessment: Every extremal C4-free graph must embed in some polarity graph of an unspecified plane/order. Finite edge counts do not obstruct embeddings into arbitrarily larger planes; no full universal obstruction.
title: McCuaig's polarity-graph conjecture for extremal $C_4$-free graphs

literal_statement:
Let $C$ be an $[n,(k_1,k_2)]$ $3$-weight code with dual minimum distance $d^\bot\ge 3$. Let its nonzero weights satisfy

$$
w_1+w_2+w_3=3n,\qquad w_1<w_2<w_3.
$$

**Middle-weight conjecture.** Then $w_2=n$.

The claim predicts that the middle nonzero weight of any such three-weight code equals the length. The supplied text does not indicate whether this conjecture has been proved or disproved.
technical_assessment: Weight sum 3n and ordered weights alone do not imply middle n. Need exact ring-linear code and dual-distance moment constraints; arbitrary triples or finite parameter codes cannot establish the universal claim.
title: The middle-weight conjecture for three-weight codes

literal_statement: Let $G$ be a graph, and let $k$ be a positive integer. **$2k$–$k/2$ conjecture.** If $\delta(G)\ge\frac{k}{2}$ and $\Delta(G)\ge2k$, then $G$ contains every tree with $k$ edges. This is a companion minimum/maximum-degree condition to the two-thirds conjecture. The source reports only approximate and bounded-maximum-degree results, so the full statement remains open.
technical_assessment: All k and every k-edge tree need a minimum/maximum-degree embedding theorem. A high-degree vertex embeds stars but not arbitrary branching; no full-scope greedy argument.
title: The $2k$–$k/2$ degree conjecture

literal_statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $\alpha\in[0,\frac13)$. **Intermediate-range conjecture.** Every graph with minimum degree at least $(1+\alpha)\frac k2$ and maximum degree at least $2(1-\alpha)k$ contains every tree with $k$ edges. This interpolates between the two degree conjectures above. The source gives partial results but no general proof.
technical_assessment: Uniformly all alpha in [0,1/3) and k interpolate two hard embedding regimes; endpoint substitution is not a full solution. No scalable extremal obstruction found.
title: The intermediate-range minimum/maximum degree conjecture

literal_statement: Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $k$ be a positive integer. **Sparse degree conjecture.** If $\delta(G)\ge\frac k2$ and at least $\frac{n}{2\sqrt{k}}$ vertices of $G$ have degree at least $k$, then $G$ contains every tree with $k$ edges. The conjecture combines the skew Loebl–Komlós–Sós perspective with minimum-degree conditions. The source presents it as new and open.
technical_assessment: The high-degree vertex fraction n/(2sqrt(k)) must force every k-edge tree with minimum degree k/2. Degree counting alone gives no arrangement control; no all-k construction or proof.
title: The sparse minimum/maximum degree conjecture for tree containment

literal_statement: A **resultant knot probability** is the proportion of crossing assignments of a free knot diagram that produce a specified knot. An **algebraic tangle** is a tangle obtained through the algebraic tangle constructions considered in the source. **Algebraic-tangle probability conjecture.** For a free knot diagram coming from algebraic tangles, the resultant figure-eight probability is less than or equal to the resultant trefoil probability. The conjecture is supported by the enumeration of free knots with at most nine crossings, but the source identifies $9_{40}$ as a counterexample when the algebraic-tangle hypothesis is omitted.
technical_assessment: All algebraic-tangle shadows and all crossing assignments require a tangle recursion preserving the probability inequality. The 9_40 counterexample drops a hypothesis and gives no eligible refutation.
title: Algebraic tangles have no more figure-eight than trefoil descendants

literal_statement: Let $k$ be a positive integer and let $[... ELLIPSIZATION...]rname{Circ}[(\ell^2-1)k,\{1,\ell\}])=2\ell. \]$ and field independent minimum rank with universally optimal matrix $A(G)$.
technical_assessment: The literal corpus statement contains the text [... ELLIPSIZATION...] and corrupted delimiters; its full quantifiers and family are unavailable. Read every available literal byte, but cannot claim a complete mathematical statement review for this row.
title: Maximum-nullity and zero-forcing equality for circulant graphs

literal_statement: Let $G$ be a planar graph on $n\geq 9$ vertices, and let $P_k$ denote the path on $k$ vertices. The join $P_2\vee P_{n-2}$ is also a planar graph. **Boots–Royle–Cao–Vince conjecture.** The planar graph on $n\geq 9$ vertices of maximum spectral radius is $P_2\vee P_{n-2}$. Tait and Tobin verified the conjecture for sufficiently large $n$, but the source states that it remains open for small $n$.
technical_assessment: All n>=9 is not reduced to a bounded certificate until an explicit effective large-n threshold and planar extremal characterization are available. No enumerated small remainder or full-scope spectral argument.
title: Boots–Royle–Cao–Vince conjecture for planar graphs

literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a compact metric space, let $r\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, and let $\mathrm{VR}_r(X)$ denote the Vietoris-Rips complex at scale $r$.

**Lower semicontinuity conjecture.** The complex $\mathrm{VR}_r(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{VR}_{r-\varepsilon}(X)$ whenever $\varepsilon>0$ is sufficiently small.

The paper explicitly labels this conjecture as false and provides a counterexample immediately afterward. Thus the proposed lower semicontinuity statement does not hold for all compact metric spaces.
technical_assessment: Literal text says the source immediately supplies a compact-metric-space counterexample. Existing counterexample would defeat eligibility; no independent primary-body inspection here.
title: Lower semicontinuity of the homotopy type of Vietoris-Rips complexes

literal_statement:
Let $(X,\mathsf{d},\mathfrak{m})$ be the RCD space under discussion, let $k=\dim(X,\mathsf{d},\mathfrak{m})$, and let $\mathcal{R}_k^*$ be the full-measure regular set. Let $\phi$ be the function defined by equation (9), and for $f\in D(\Delta)$ let $\mathrm{Hess}_f$ be its Hessian. **Differentiability and weighted Laplacian conjecture.** The function $\phi$ is differentiable for $\mathfrak{m}$-almost every $x\in\mathcal{R}_k^*$. Moreover, for every $f\in D(\Delta)$,

$$
\Delta f(x)=\operatorname{tr}(\mathrm{Hess}_f)(x)+\langle\nabla\log\phi,\nabla f\rangle(x)
$$

holds for $\mathfrak{m}$-almost every $x\in X$. This is the paper's final conjecture, giving a pointwise weighted correction to the Laplacian–Hessian trace identity; the supplied context gives no resolution.
technical_assessment: Almost-everywhere differentiability of source-defined phi and the identity for every Laplacian-domain f require RCD regularity tools. Smooth weighted manifolds verify only a special case; phi equation9 is needed.
title: Differentiability and weighted Laplacian formula on RCD spaces

literal_statement:
Let $V$ be a self-dual integral form of the monster vertex algebra, let $g$ be a Fricke element, and suppose that $g^j$ is a Fricke element for every integer $j>0$. **Weaker Borcherds vanishing conjecture.** Then

$$
\hat{H}^1(g,V)=0.
$$

This is proposed as a weaker version of Borcherds's conjecture on the vanishing of $hat{H}^1(g,V)$. The paper gives a counterexample to the stronger vanishing claim for all Fricke elements, while this restricted formulation is presented as a conjecture and its resolution is not supplied here.
technical_assessment: The stronger Fricke claim's counterexample need not satisfy every positive power being Fricke. Need exact integral Monster form and Tate computation within this restriction; no small independent certificate.
title: Weaker Borcherds conjecture on vanishing of Tate cohomology for Fricke elements

literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a $K_5$-minor free graph with maximum degree $\Delta=6$.

**Edge-coloring conjecture.** Then $G$ is class $1$.

This conjecture extends the paper's result that every $K_5$-minor free graph with maximum degree at least $7$ is class $1$, and asks whether the analogous conclusion holds at maximum degree six.
technical_assessment: At maximum degree exactly6, the >=7 theorem gives no implication. Need six-edge-coloring for every K5-minor-free graph, including nonplanar clique-sum pieces; no short reduction established.
title: Class 1 conjecture for $K_5$-minor free graphs of maximum degree six

literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal D_n$ be the average number of iterations of the stack-sorting map needed to sort a permutation in $S_n$ into the identity permutation. **Strengthened West conjecture.** The limit

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\mathcal D_n}{n}
$$

exists and lies in the interval $(0.77,0.81)$. This strengthens West's conjecture by proposing numerical bounds in addition to existence; the source gives numerical evidence but no proof.
technical_assessment: Existence of an all-n average-depth limit and strict numerical interval cannot follow from finite permutations. No concentration/subadditivity mechanism established; keep separate from parked different stack-fiber family.
title: Strengthened West conjecture for average stack-sorting depth

literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a bipartite graph, and let $\chi'_S(G)$ denote its strong chromatic index and $\Delta(G)$ its maximum degree.

**Faudree et al.'s conjecture.**

$$
\chi'_S(G)\leq \Delta(G)^2.
$$

The bound is tight for complete bipartite graphs with appropriate part sizes. It is known for graphs whose cycle lengths are all divisible by $4$ and for $\Delta(G)=3$, but remains open in general.
technical_assessment: All bipartite graphs need Delta^2 induced-matchings decomposition. Greedy coloring of the squared line graph gives a weaker constant; complete bipartite equality is a known parameter family only.
title: Faudree et al.'s bipartite strong chromatic index conjecture

literal_statement:
Let $\bm{U}_n$ denote the vector of oriented swap process finishing times and let $\bm{V}_n$ denote the point-to-line last passage percolation vector. **The oriented swap process–LPP conjecture.** For all $n\geq 2$,

$$
\bm{U}_n \overset{D}{=} \bm{V}_n.
$$

The equality is conjectural and remains mysterious; the paper gives an algebraic-combinatorial reformulation and proves related marginal identities, but does not establish the full vector-valued distributional identity.
technical_assessment: All n>=2 joint finishing-time laws need more than marginal identities. Integrable-probability successors may resolve the vector law; no body clearance or new coupling supplied.
title: The oriented swap process–last passage percolation distributional identity

literal_statement:
For a square $\pm1$ matrix $M$, define $\operatorname{Res}(M)$ to be the minimum number of entries that must be switched from $1$ to $-1$ or vice versa to make $M$ singular.

**Rank-resilience conjecture.** With probability $1-o(1)$,

$$
\operatorname{Res}(M_n)=\left(\frac12+o(1)\right)n.
$$

The source notes a partial result but does not report a resolution of the conjecture.
technical_assessment: High-probability lower bound after adversarial entry flips requires uniform singularity control over exponentially many perturbations. Making two rows equal suggests an upper bound only; no matching lower-bound route.
title: The rank-resilience conjecture for random sign matrices

literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite nilpotent group, let $w$ be a word in $k$ variables, and define $N_w(g)$ to be the number of tuples $(g_1,\ldots,g_k)\in G^{(k)}$ satisfying $w(g_1,\ldots,g_k)=g$. Let $G_w$ denote the image of the word map $w\colon G^{(k)}\to G$. **Generalized Amit conjecture.** For every $g\in G_w$, one has

$$
N_w(g)\geq |G|^{k-1}.
$$

This strengthens Amit's conjecture from the identity fibre to every nonempty fibre of the word map. The source records that the identity case and several special classes of words are known, while the generalized assertion is presented as a version under consideration and remains open.
technical_assessment: Every finite nilpotent group, word and nonempty fiber requires a uniform lower bound. Abelian homomorphism fibers have equal sizes but do not settle nonabelian nilpotent groups; no bounded certificate construction.
title: Generalized Amit conjecture for fibres of word maps

literal_statement:
Let $v_0$ be a null vector and let $N_k,q_k$ be the charge data entering the pairings

$$
b^{\,0}_{k\ell}=v_0\cdot(N_kq_{\ell}-N_{\ell}q_k).
$$

Assume that all $b^{\,0}_{k\ell}$ are nonzero. Let $\Phi_n$ be the function defined in the source, and let ${\rm Sym}$ denote the stated symmetrization. **The sign-identity conjecture.** The function

$$
F_n(\{\check\gamma_i\},y)={\rm Sym}\left\{y^{\sum_{i<j}\gamma_{ij}}\Phi_n(\{\check\gamma_i\})\right\}
$$

has a zero of order $n-1$ at $y=1$. The conjecture is intended to supply the vanishing required in the unrefined limit, but no proof is given for all cases in the source.
technical_assessment: Order n-1 vanishing is equivalent to n-1 derivative identities, but Phi_n and source symmetrization are not explicit here. Checking low n cannot prove every charge configuration; no combinatorial cancellation supplied.
title: The sign-identity conjecture for the theta-series kernel

literal_statement: Let a complex structure determine a Fukaya category, and let special Lagrangians be the relevant geometric objects in that category. **Stability conjecture.** Complex structures are stability conditions for Fukaya categories, and special Lagrangians are stable. This is described as a folklore conjecture motivated by the work of Thomas and Yau; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
technical_assessment: The record does not specify a precise stability-condition space or Fukaya-category hypotheses. A folklore slogan cannot support a literal formal endpoint; no full-scope route.
title: Stability conjecture for special Lagrangians in Fukaya categories

literal_statement:
Let a spherical cap have radius $\alpha$, and let it be covered by a collection of convex spherical domains. For each domain, let its inradius be the radius of its largest inscribed spherical cap.

**Cap covering inradius conjecture.** The sum of the inradii of all domains in the collection is at least $\alpha$.

This problem is known for $\alpha\geq \pi/2$ but remains open for $\alpha<\pi/2$.
technical_assessment: For every cap covering by convex spherical domains need an inradius-sum bound even below pi/2. Great-circle plank arguments for larger caps do not directly control these small-cap covers.
title: Cap covering inradius conjecture

literal_statement: Let $T$ be a minimum weighted Szeged index tree, rooted at its designated root. **Root-to-leaf degree conjecture.** Along every path from the root to a leaf, the sequence of vertex degrees is non-increasing. This is one of the paper's experimentally motivated structural conjectures for minimum weighted Szeged index trees, and its resolution is left open.
technical_assessment: Universal degree monotonicity in global minimum weighted-Szeged trees requires an exchange inequality valid for all branch sizes. Root designation and objective must be sourced; no finite sweep substitutes for the exchange.
title: Non-increasing root-to-leaf degrees in minimum weighted Szeged index trees

literal_statement: Let $T$ be a minimum weighted Szeged index tree. **Maximum-degree conjecture.** No vertex of $T$ has degree greater than $6$. This is an experimentally motivated structural conjecture intended to constrain minimum weighted Szeged index trees; the paper does not report a proof or disproof.
technical_assessment: Every minimizing tree would need a degree<=6 exchange proof independent of order. Finite tree enumeration supplies instances only; no all-branch reduction demonstrated.
title: Degree bound for vertices in minimum weighted Szeged index trees

literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface, and let $C\subseteq X$ be a curve. Denote by $\mathcal O_X(C)$ the associated line bundle and by $h^i(\mathcal O_X(C))$ its cohomology dimensions.

**Bounding cohomology conjecture.** There exists a constant $c_X>0$ such that

$$
h^1(\mathcal O_X(C))\leq c_Xh^0(\mathcal O_X(C))
$$

for every curve $C$ on $X$.

This conjecture is stronger than the bounded negativity conjecture and was the main problem studied in the source. It has been disproved: a counterexample exists on a smooth projective surface with large Picard number.
technical_assessment: Literal record reports a smooth-projective large-Picard-number counterexample to the uniform cohomology ratio. No novel surface construction or source-body proof checked here.
title: The bounding cohomology conjecture for smooth projective surfaces

literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected $Delta$-regular graph of order $n$ for some $Delta geq 3$.

**Baste–Fürst–Henning–Mohr–Rautenbach conjecture.**

$$
\gamma(G) \leq \frac{2\Delta-1}{4\Delta}n + \frac{1}{2}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the edge domination number of connected regular graphs and would give a sharp general upper bound for minimum maximal matchings.
technical_assessment: All Delta>=3 connected regular graphs require a small maximal matching, not merely a small maximum matching. Greedy maximal matching gives only a weaker bound; no structural induction meeting the coefficient.
title: Baste–Fürst–Henning–Mohr–Rautenbach bound for minimum maximal matchings

literal_statement: Let $\mathfrak{S}_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $\overline{\gamma}$ denote the complement-inversion Foatic action on $\mathfrak{S}_n$. For a permutation $w$, let $\operatorname{Fix}(w)$ be the number of fixed points, or 1-cycles, of $w$. **Complement-inversion fixed-point homomesy conjecture.** The statistic $\operatorname{Fix}$ is 1-mesic on every orbit of the action of $\overline{\gamma}$. Computations for $n\leq 11$ found no counterexample, while the source states that the general claim remains unproved.
technical_assessment: Every complement-inversion Foatic orbit requires a fixed-point coboundary or involution; n<=11 supplies no all-n orbit identity. Exact Foatic action needed before any exhaustive check.
title: Fixed-point homomesy conjecture for the complement-inversion Foatic action

literal_statement:
Let $P_i$ denote the path graph with $i$ vertices, and let $\square$ denote the Cartesian product of graphs. For $i\leq j$ with $i,j\in\mathbb{Z}_{>1}$, consider $P_i\square P_j$. A graph has the **complete maximal identity property** if its maximal stable configuration is equivalent to the identity for every choice of sink.

**Path-product conjecture.** The only graphs $P_i\square P_j$ with the complete maximal identity property are $P_2\square P_j$ when $j\equiv1\pmod{3}$, together with $P_2\square P_2$, which is $K_4$.

The conjecture was supported by a SageMath verification for $1<i\leq j\leq100$. The proposition establishing the listed $P_2\square P_j$ cases is proved in the paper, but the exclusion of all other path products remains open.
technical_assessment: Primary v1 Conjecture6.2 and Proposition6.1 concern strong products, not Cartesian products. Read Proposition6.1 proof. Cartesian P2 square P2 is C4, not K4; correcting the record earns no discovery credit. No resolution of the genuine strong-product conjecture claimed.
title: Complete maximal identity conjecture for Cartesian products of paths

literal_statement:
Let $T_r({\bf x}^m)$ be the symmetric polynomials defined in the source's formula (j13), and let $T_1({\bf x}^m)$ be the first polynomial in this family. **Binomial recurrence conjecture.** For every integer $n$ satisfying $1\leq n\leq m/2$,

$$
\frac{T_{2n-1}({\bf x}^m)}{T_1^{2n-1}({\bf x}^m)}=\sum_{k=1}^{2n-1}(-1)^{k+1}{2n-1\choose k}\frac{T_{2n-1-k}({\bf x}^m)}{T_1^{2n-1-k}({\bf x}^m)}.
$$

The identity is motivated by its agreement with the corresponding integer-coefficient formulas for the cases $n=2,3,4$; whether it holds in the stated generality is left unresolved in the supplied source.
technical_assessment: Primary v1 Eq13 defines T_r as moments of a sum of independent uniforms via inclusion-exclusion; central symmetry yields the displayed odd-moment binomial identity. v1 Conjecture2 instead asks positive integer coefficients after eliminating odd moments. Need exact later-version mapping and successor bodies; elementary moment adaptation would earn no credit.
title: Binomial recurrence conjecture for the symmetric polynomials $T_r$

literal_statement: Let $h_=h\Psi$ be the element defined in the last remark before the appendix of Dotsenko, Shadrin, and Vallette (2016). Let $i_$ and $p_$ be the $_\alpha$-morphisms whose composite is $i_\circledcirc p_$, and let $\mathrm{id}$ denote the identity $_\alpha$-morphism. **Gauge homotopy equivalence conjecture.** The element $h_=h\Psi$ is a gauge homotopy equivalence of $_\alpha$-morphisms between $i_\circledcirc p_$ and $\mathrm{id}$. This conjecture concerns the economical gauge-homotopy notion for infinity-morphisms introduced in the paper; its validity is not resolved in the supplied text.
technical_assessment: The gauge homotopy hPsi and infinity-morphism composition depend on a substantial transfer/operad framework missing from the record. No short endpoint or independent algebraic route supplied.
title: Gauge homotopy equivalence of the homotopy inverse composite

literal_statement:
A **knot projection** is the image of a generic immersion of a circle into the $2$-sphere, and deformations of types $1$, $2$, and $3$ are the local replacements analogous to Reidemeister moves. In particular, consider generic immersions

$$
S^{1}\to\mathbb{R}^{2}
$$

and embeddings of the circle. **Östlund's conjecture.** Deformations of types $1$ and $3$ are sufficient to obtain a homotopy from any generic immersion $S^{1}\to\mathbb{R}^{2}$ to an embedding. The conjecture was disproved by Hagge and Yazinski, who exhibited a first counterexample with $16$ double points; consequently, deformations of type $2$ can be necessary.
technical_assessment: Literal text reports Hagge-Yazinski's published sixteen-double-point counterexample. Reconstructing it is known-result formalization, not eligible discovery; no body audit here.
title: Östlund's conjecture on simplifying generic circle immersions

literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $\Delta$ be its maximum degree, and let $\mathrm{HG}(G)$ denote its hat-guessing number.

**Maximum-degree hat-guessing conjecture.**

$$
\mathrm{HG}(G)\leq \Delta+1.
$$

This conjecture tightens the folklore upper bound $e\Delta$ obtained from the Lovász Local Lemma and is supported by the results in the paper. It was first proposed in the cited work, but remains open.
technical_assessment: HG<=Delta+1 is the same apparent full-scope maximum-degree hat-game question as assigned342673. Local-lemma eDelta does not imply it; no separate credit or new strategy obstruction.
title: Maximum-degree bound for the hat-guessing number
